Quickstart

Stripe's APIs power a wide range of online payment flows. The quickstart introduces the core concepts: PaymentIntents for handling payments, Customers for reusable billing, and webhooks for asynchronous events. Following this guide end-to-end will get you from zero to a working test charge in roughly ten minutes.

Install the SDK

Use your package manager of choice. The official Stripe SDKs cover most server-side languages and follow semantic versioning so upgrades are predictable. Pin a major version in your manifest to keep deployments deterministic across environments. 

npm install stripe

Authenticate requests

All Stripe API calls require a secret key passed via the Authorization header. Use a restricted key in production so that compromised credentials cannot perform sensitive operations. Rotate keys via the dashboard at least once per quarter, or immediately after any incident. 

export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...

Create a test charge

In test mode you can use Stripe's standard test card numbers to simulate any payment outcome without moving real money. Each card maps to a deterministic response — success, decline, insufficient funds, fraud — so you can exercise every code path in your integration tests.
